newsitem.title: USA: U S West sells Time Warner shares - Variety.
newsitem.headline: U S West sells Time Warner shares - Variety.

text.p: U S West has sold its shareholding stake in Time Warner Inc as chances of restructuring their partnership appear to be waning, Daily Variety reported in Thursday's edition.

U S West sold its holding of 4.4 million shares in Time Warner to Salomon Bros, which was in the process of re-selling the stock to institutional investors Wednesday night, Wall Street sources told Variety.
U S West sold it at a closing price on Wednesday of $50 per share, making the block worth $225 million.
Neither Time Warner nor U S West would comment on the move.

The sale came the same day that the Wall Street Journal reported that Time Warner Vice Chairman Ted Turner had been telling the financial community that the company was re-evaluating its plan to restructure the Time Warner Entertainment partnership and might not go through with it.
U S West owns 25.5 percent of the partnership, and the two companies have spent much of the past two years in periodic negotiations trying to agree on a deal for the restructuring.
